note: Read RFC7911 Section 2 and all current tagged carriers. Colliding sources must remain distinct for the same native prefix, while replacements and inverse withdrawals retain the locally generated association. Current assertions cover received identifiers zero and maximum, occupied wrap candidates, unframed ingress, independent destinations, IPv4 same/cross-context conversion, and IPv6 MP_REACH/MP_UNREACH same-context, cross-context and unframed-source conversion. The changed probe checks exact prefix/identifier pairing and that retiring one prefix cannot renumber another using the same ingress identifier. Churn carriers drive reactorForwardRS through actual destination writes and cache eviction, including rebuilt reflection frames and a mixed withdraw/reannounce; they check exact recipient-visible identities rather than treating internal table counts as the RFC obligation. The foreign FRR checker separately requires two source-attributed paths with distinct identifiers and stable replay; the functional carrier separately checks live/replay wire framing. Its pinned zero is a deterministic fixture expectation, not an RFC allocation rule. The allocator, rewrite, rebuilt SourceID preservation, release boundary and raw/converted writer consumers were traced. No residual whole-clause gap identified. Incremental independent rejudgment, 2026-10-22, after the recipient-owned lifetime and staged-collision fixes. Read the actual RFC 7911 Sections 2 and 5, all current carriers named by the existing audit for these two requirements, their relevant helpers, and producer/consumer boundaries. Section 2: "However, the Path Identifier MUST be assigned in such a way that the BGP speaker is able to use the (Prefix, Path Identifier) to uniquely identify a path advertised to a neighbor." Section 2: "A BGP speaker that re-advertises a route MUST generate its own Path Identifier to be associated with the re-advertised route." Section 5: "In particular, a new advertisement for a given address prefix and a given Path Identifier replaces a previous advertisement for the same address prefix and Path Identifier." Section 5: "If a BGP speaker receives a message to withdraw a prefix with a Path Identifier not seen before, it SHOULD silently ignore it." The source allocator now counts source mappings, recorded recipient slots and temporary proposals independently. Cache eviction drops only the mapping reference. Final ownership admission resolves the preserved ingress source/received-identifier/native-prefix key through adjRIBOut.sourcePaths, patches only the session-private buffer, and retains an already advertised identity for both replacement and withdrawal. New colliding announcements reserve a distinct ID; importantly, bindSourcePath also retains every noncolliding staged proposal, so a later collision in the same UPDATE cannot mint its ID after mapping eviction and counter wrap. Bindings survive both ownership-filter passes and release after record/refusal; installed slots retain separately, ownership replacement removes stale ingress bindings, deletion/session clear releases slot references, and write failure retires the session. prepareFwdProvenance and writePath preserve the incoming association; both rawBodies and converted updates dispatch through fwdBatchHandler into the common writeUpdateBody admission before PATHS-LIMIT and final recording. These are actual producer code guards, not added tagged evidence. No assertion or RFC claim was changed for this rejudgment.
